title: Second Call for Applications Under ₹5,000 Crore PRIP Scheme to Boost Pharma & MedTech Innovation announced
subtitle: PRIP Scheme Opens New Opportunities for Startups, MSMEs and Industry Across Priority Pharma & MedTech Areas
body_text:
The Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers has announced the second call for applications under the Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech (PRIP) Scheme. The Scheme with a financial outlay of ₹ 5,000 crore aims to strengthen India’s Pharma and MedTech research and development ecosystem by supporting startups, MSMEs, and large companies to leapfrog up the innovation value chain.
Applications are invited across two tracks:
Early stage: Projects of startups and MSMEs to take products or technologies at TRL (Technology Readiness Level) 1, 2 or 3 in any priority area to higher TRLs not beyond TRL 5 will be eligible. These projects will follow a two-stage process, beginning with a concise Concept Note, followed by a detailed application for shortlisted applicants. Concept Notes can be submitted directly by eligible MSMEs and startups, or by ecosystem enablers on behalf of promising projects within their networks. Financial assistance to the extent of ₹5 crore per project will be provided under the scheme. Later stage: Projects of industry, startups and MSMEs to take products or technologies at TRL 4, 5, or 6 in any priority area to higher TRLs will be eligible. Late-stage projects can apply directly through the detailed application form. Financial assistance to the extent of ₹100 crore per project will be provided under the scheme subject to the condition that such assistance will be restricted to a maximum of 35% of the approved total project cost and the remainder of the approved total project cost will be co-funded by the applicant.
Application forms and supporting guidance are available on the PRIP portal: https://prip.pharma-dept.gov.in/ . Applicants can also refer to the following resources for details on the application requirements:
Scheme documents: Scheme and Scheme Guidelines Concept note (for early-stage projects): Guidance for Concept Note Detailed application form (for later-stage projects) : Guidance for Application Form Other documents: Milestone Descriptor Catalogue and Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) For additional guidance on various aspects of the scheme, please refer to the Application Support Toolkit .
The submission window on PRIP portal will open by mid-September. Applicants who had submitted projects under PRIP Round 1  have been asked not to resubmit the same project. For any queries, interested applicants can write to support-prip@pharma-dept.gov.in.
PRIP scheme was launched in 2023 with a view to promote research and development in the Pharmaceutical sector, including in the areas of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning. It seeks to  build world-class research infrastructure and deepen the talent pool of qualified, trained students. With a view to enhance the prospects of commercialisation of viable outputs, industry and startups can also take advantage of mentorship support that will be provided under the Scheme. Initiatives such as MedTech Mitra and Patent Mitra and the online platform under the Scheme will facilitate collaboration and partnership among various stakeholders.
Following are the identified priority areas under the scheme.
1. New Medicines – new chemical medicines/substances (including new chemical Entity (NCE), New Biological Entity (NBE) and Phyto-pharmaceuticals)
2. Complex Generics and Biosimilars
3. Novel medical devices (Targeted Innovative Therapeutics) - This refers to medical devices that have not been previously approved by CDSCO. It covers all novel medical devices, including the following: (i) AI/ML based medical devices with software development, Software as Medical Device (SaMD) and Software in Medical Device (SiMD); (ii) Medical diagnostics and screening devices with genetic technology;  (iii) Robotic medical devices for surgical procedures; (iv) Medical devices with telemedicine facilities; and (v) Any novel in vitro diagnostic medical device, including biomarkers, that enables precision medicine.

enrichment.summary: The Department of Pharmaceuticals has opened the second call for applications under the ₹5,000 crore PRIP (Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech) Scheme, inviting startups, MSMEs and industry to apply across two tracks: early-stage projects (TRL 1-3 to TRL 5, up to ₹5 crore support) and later-stage projects (TRL 4-6 upward, up to ₹100 crore support capped at 35% of project cost). The submission window on the PRIP portal opens by mid-September, and applicants from Round 1 are asked not to resubmit the same project.
enrichment.context:
PRIP was launched in 2023 to boost India's pharmaceutical and medical technology R&D ecosystem, aiming to move the country up the innovation value chain from being primarily a generics manufacturer towards developing new chemical/biological entities, complex generics, biosimilars and novel medical devices, including AI/ML-based diagnostics and robotic surgical devices. It complements other government efforts to strengthen domestic innovation capacity, such as the National Biopharma Mission and PLI schemes for pharmaceuticals and medical devices, and reflects India's broader push for self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) in critical health technologies amid dependence on imported APIs and high-end medical devices.

The scheme's structure—supporting projects through Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) with graded early- and late-stage funding, co-funding requirements for larger grants, and support mechanisms like MedTech Mitra and Patent Mitra for mentorship and IP facilitation—illustrates a shift in government funding philosophy from pure subsidy to risk-sharing partnership with industry. This second call indicates the scheme has moved from initial rollout into a sustained funding cycle, which aspirants should note as part of India's evolving pharma/biotech innovation policy landscape.

prelims_questions.question: The 'PRIP Scheme', recently in news, pertains to which of the following?
options: Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech
Public Reforms in Insurance and Pensions
prelims_questions.explanation: PRIP stands for Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech, a ₹5,000 crore scheme by the Department of Pharmaceuticals to boost R&D in the pharma and medtech sectors.

prelims_questions.question: In the context of the PRIP Scheme, 'TRL' refers to:
prelims_questions.explanation: TRL (Technology Readiness Level) is a scale used to assess the maturity of a technology, and PRIP uses it to categorize projects into early-stage (TRL 1-5) and later-stage (TRL 4 and above) funding tracks.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of risk-sharing, co-funded innovation schemes like PRIP in strengthening India's pharmaceutical and medical technology research ecosystem. What challenges must be addressed for such schemes to translate into commercially viable innovations?

India remains heavily dependent on imports for high-end medical devices and active pharmaceutical ingredients despite being a major generic drug manufacturer. Examine the role of government schemes in bridging this innovation gap.

study_notes.reason: The release is primarily a factual announcement of scheme parameters (funding tracks, TRL thresholds, financial caps) rather than a policy debate; the analytical angle on innovation-financing philosophy is present but thin, so the study value skews toward memorisable facts.

prelims.point: PRIP (Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech) Scheme has a ₹5,000 crore outlay, was launched in 2023, and is administered by the Department of Pharmaceuticals under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
prelims.why_important: Basic scheme identity (name, ministry, outlay, launch year) is classic objective-question material.

prelims.point: PRIP funds two tracks by Technology Readiness Level (TRL): early-stage (TRL 1-3 up to TRL 5, up to ₹5 crore support) and later-stage (TRL 4-6 upward, up to ₹100 crore support capped at 35% of approved project cost, remainder co-funded by applicant).
prelims.why_important: UPSC often tests numerical/structural distinctions between funding tiers of a scheme, and TRL is a recurring science-policy concept worth knowing precisely.

prelims.point: MedTech Mitra and Patent Mitra are support mechanisms under PRIP providing mentorship and IP-facilitation to applicants.
prelims.why_important: Naming and function of scheme sub-components are typical distractor material in statement-based questions.

mains.point: PRIP's co-funding requirement for later-stage projects (govt funds capped at 35%) marks a shift in government support philosophy from pure subsidy to risk-sharing partnership with industry.
mains.theme: Innovation financing and public-private risk sharing
mains.analytical_use: Useful for a question on evaluating changing models of government support for R&D/innovation, or examining India's approach to de-risking private investment in high-cost sectors.

mains.point: The scheme aims to move India up the pharma/medtech value chain from a generics-manufacturing base toward new chemical/biological entities and novel medical devices, addressing import dependence on APIs and high-end devices.
mains.analytical_use: Can support answers on self-reliance in critical health technologies or on strategies to reduce import dependence in pharmaceuticals and medical devices.
